strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the tension between real-world limited data and synthetic data with sim-to-real gap; the proposed multi-expert VLA combination is intuitive
Comprehensive simulation experiments with thorough ablation studies validating capability-balanced data aggregation, online training iterations, and multi-expert combination strategies
Multi-view 360° perception effectively addresses FOV limitations of single-camera methods; clear quantitative improvements across reaching, squeezing, and avoiding scenarios

Practical systems contribution: achieves ~7 Hz inference with 7B LLM on multi-view input, suitable for real deployment; VLA student outperforms individual RL teachers demonstrating effective knowledge integration
Novel capability-balanced data aggregation method with clear ablation showing faster convergence and more stable training compared to unbalanced data
Real-world deployment on Unitree GO2 demonstrating sim-to-real transfer in challenging scenarios (thin obstacles, crowded environments, transparent objects)
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: multi-view VLA extension is straightforward, DAgger is well-established; main contribution is engineering existing techniques together rather than novel methodology

Critical missing baselines: no comparison with recent VLA-based navigation methods (Uni-NaVid, NaVid, TrackVLA) despite mentioning them in related work; only compares against single-view imitation learning methods

Weak real-world validation: only qualitative demonstrations without quantitative metrics (SR, CR, WTT); impossible to assess sim-to-real performance gap or validate robustness claims; no real-world comparison with baselines

Insufficient analysis of mechanism: paper claims 'synergistic effect' but provides limited insight into why VLA outperforms RL experts; missing ablation on multi-view vs single-view data from same experts
Hyperparameter choices lack justification: loss weight β=5, smoothing α=0.3, ε=0.1, and reward coefficients not ablated or justified; no sensitivity analysis despite significant impact on results

Generalization claims not fully supported: intentionally reduced difficulty in Mixed scene's squeezing segment undermines testing; evaluation primarily on variations of same three capabilities within same simulator
Data efficiency not analyzed: requires 500k+steps for training; no minimum data analysis or sample efficiency comparison with baselines; scalability to new capabilities unclear

Missing critical ablations: no validation of QA data contribution, no multi-view vs single-view comparison with same training data, no justification of architectural choices (history window length, projector design)
Incomplete technical specification: multi-view token combination method not clearly specified; limited details on VLA architecture modifications for multi-view inputs
Reproducibility concerns: missing implementation details, no code availability mentioned, expensive training (40 GPU hours) with unclear necessity, scattered hyperparameter choices

strengths: Well-motivated capability-balanced training strategy that addresses the practical problem of uneven performance across multiple navigation skills, demonstrated through clear empirical results (Figure 4 showing convergence across capabilities)

Strong empirical performance with 88.1% success rate on InternVLA-N1 System-1 benchmark, substantially outperforming prior methods (25% improvement over strongest RGB-D baseline), with validation on multiple custom IsaacLab scenarios

Comprehensive real-world validation across diverse scenarios (Thin Wire Avoidance, Clustered Corridor, Pedestrian Avoidance, Outdoor Alley) demonstrating practical sim-to-real transfer with effective obstacle handling
Thoughtful 360° multi-view design enabling spatial awareness in constrained environments while maintaining 7 Hz inference speed for practical deployment
Large-scale training data collection (1.5M expert demonstrations) with multi-expert learning from specialized RL policies, providing substantial supervision for each navigation capability
Meaningful ablation studies examining multi-view contributions, VQA data impact, capability-balancing effectiveness, and expert combination strategies with clear performance comparisons
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—primarily an engineering combination of existing techniques (multi-expert learning, VQA training, VLA models) without significant methodological innovation; the core capability-balanced aggregation is a relatively straightforward heuristic weighted sampling approach

Weak theoretical justification for design choices: Equation 6's weighting scheme lacks formal analysis, smoothing factor α=0.3 appears arbitrary with minimal ablation, and velocity control parameterization uses ad-hoc constraints without principled justification

Unclear VQA data contribution—while Figure 5(b) shows ~20% performance drop without VQA, the ablation cannot distinguish whether improvements come from VQA data itself versus general multi-task learning benefits; limited analysis of learned visual-language understanding

Real-world evaluation limited in scope: only 4 scenarios on a single robot platform (Unitree GO2) with 20 trials each, no systematic failure mode analysis, and no evaluation on robots with different sensor configurations, raising questions about generalization

Synthetic environments lack visual diversity—IsaacLab scenes use basic geometric obstacles with minimal texture/lighting variation compared to real-world complexity, limiting validity of sim-to-real gap assessment

Narrow baseline comparisons: InternVLA-N1 benchmark primarily includes RGB-D methods and outdated baselines (NavDP, SIDP from 2021); missing comparisons with recent end-to-end VLA models from 2024-2025 (Qwen2-VL variants, COME-robot, etc.)

Architecture design choices not justified: no ablation on 7B model scale, no justification for specific VLA backbone selection, sensitivity to design choices unexplored; 360° camera setup is specific with unclear generalization to alternative sensor configurations

Reproducibility concerns: collecting 1.5M expert demonstrations is resource-intensive, VQA dataset filtering criteria incompletely specified, hyperparameter choices appear tuned per-capability without systematic justification, no code/data release plans mentioned

Insufficient analysis of learning dynamics: Figure 4 shows unexpected WTT increase after finetuning without clear explanation; Figure 7 capability-convergence mechanism unexplained; no analysis of which skills transfer best/worst

Dense presentation with critical implementation details (reward coefficients Table 4, PPO hyperparameters Table 6) scattered across main paper and appendix, making it difficult to distinguish novelty from standard practice
